incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act (As Revised) of the Cayman Islands, Parts I and VI; Tax Concessions Act (Cap. 117), s. 6; Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, ss. 347-383 (external company registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry (Companies Registrar); Companies House Gibraltar for external registration
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Cayman: Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Application for Incorporation of an Exempted Company; Gibraltar: Application for Registration as an External Company under the Companies Act 2014
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital. The Cayman Exempted Company may be incorporated with a single no-par-value share or no issued capital. No escrow account or capital deposit is required. For Gibraltar external registration, no local capital requirement applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS IN WRITING OF THE SUBSCRIBERS/SOLE DIRECTOR OF [COMPANY NAME], a Cayman exempted company, dated [DATE]. WHEREAS the Company has been incorporated under the Companies Act (As Revised); and the subscribers/directors have considered the matters set out below. IT IS RESOLVED: (1) The subscription of [NUMBER] ordinary shares of no par value be accepted and such shares are allotted as fully paid. (2) The registered office of the Company be established at [REGISTERED AGENT ADDRESS], Cayman Islands, and that office be maintained as the statutory registered office. (3) [NAME] be appointed sole director and [NAME] be appointed secretary, with authority to execute banking, tax and corporate filings and to engage professional advisers. This resolution shall be effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage a licensed Cayman Islands registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute an engagement letter with the licensed registered agent, complete KYC/AML due diligence forms, provide source-of-funds evidence and beneficial ownership details, and confirm that the statutory registered office will be maintained at the agent's Cayman Islands address.
required_dossiers: Certified passports of all directors and shareholders
Proof of residential address of each director/shareholder
Corporate constitutional documents if a corporate shareholder is used
AML/KYC questionnaire completed by each principal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agent requires enhanced due diligence, provide notarised bank statements and independent legal references, or substitute another CIMA-licensed registered agent and re-submit the engagement file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Memorandum and Articles of Association with the Cayman Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry, Companies Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed Memorandum and Articles of Association in English to the Registrar together with the registered agent's consent, statement of directors and officers particulars, and the applicable government registration fee. The company must be designated as an exempted company and may adopt no-par-value shares.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association executed by the subscriber
Registered office consent letter from the licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the constitutional documents, file an amended memorandum or a supplementary declaration within 7 calendar days and pay any expedited correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and tax exemption undertaking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry; Cayman Islands Ministry of Financial Services for tax concession
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, submit a tax exemption application under section 6 of the Tax Concessions Act (Cap. 117) to obtain a 20-year undertaking from the Cayman Islands government exempting the company from direct taxation. The certificate and tax undertaking are then held by the registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax exemption certificate is delayed or queried, provide certified non-resident ownership declarations and amend the memorandum to ensure no domestic business is carried on in the Cayman Islands.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint officers, adopt first board resolutions and open payment/EMI accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors; company secretary; CIMA-regulated bank or EMI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pass the pro forma first board resolution in writing, ratify the share subscription, adopt the registered office and appoint officers. File the resolutions and register of members with the registered agent. Then open an operational account with Stripe, Paddle or a Gibraltar/UK EMI for payment processing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and constitutional documents
Payment processor onboarding forms for Stripe and Paddle
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or EMI raises AML concerns, provide an independent legal opinion and audited financial projections, or apply to an alternative CIMA-regulated financial institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register as an external company in Gibraltar (elective GI presence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the Cayman company establishes a place of business or holds contracts/assets in Gibraltar, submit an application for registration as an external company under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014. Provide certified copies of the Cayman incorporation documents, a Gibraltar registered office, and a Gibraltar-resident person authorised to accept service of process.
required_dossiers: Certified Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent of Gibraltar-resident person authorised to accept service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Companies House Gibraltar queries the certified copies or translation, provide a notarised English translation and UK apostille; if no physical place of business exists, withdraw the external registration and rely solely on remote digital service arrangements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - software-only remote screen-sharing and IoT telemetry services do not trigger an industrial licensing board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no operating, manufacturing or industrial permit is required for ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 remote access and telemetry software.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Gibraltar Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change (advisory only; no EIA triggered)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - full EIA not required for zero-emission, remote software operations; no physical industrial installation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - no wastewater, VOC or hazardous waste generation. If a physical Gibraltar office is later opened, it must comply with Gibraltar Water (Discharges) Regulations, waste management standards, and energy efficiency requirements for commercial premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for home/remote-only operations. If a physical Gibraltar branch is established, obtain fire safety certification from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service, structural load approval from Building Control, and a workplace risk assessment under applicable occupational safety and health regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar. Official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation-and-financial-services. Indirect tax (Purchase Tax and customs duties) is administered by the Customs and Excise Department, HM Government of Gibraltar (https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/customs). The Cayman Islands General Registry is the company registrar in the home jurisdiction; no Cayman direct tax authority exists because the Cayman Islands imposes no income tax, corporation tax, or capital gains tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The KY_EXEMPTED_CO, as a Cayman Exempted Company, receives no Cayman TIN because Cayman has no direct tax registration. To operate in or from Gibraltar with a statutory tax presence, the entity must first register as an oversea company with Companies House Gibraltar using the Overseas Company Registration application (Form F-0). The submission must include the Cayman certificate of incorporation, certified memorandum and articles of association, a current certificate of good standing from the Cayman Registrar of Companies, particulars of directors and secretary, a Gibraltar registered office address, and the appointment of a Gibraltar-licensed corporate or individual agent. Upon acceptance, the Income Tax Office assigns a Gibraltar Tax Returns Number (TRN). For Gibraltar Purchase Tax, a separate Customs registration is required only for importation of physical goods into Gibraltar; cross-border remote software services do not trigger Purchase Tax registration. No Gibraltar VAT identification number can be obtained because Gibraltar is not within the EU or UK VAT area. If the entity uses Paddle or Stripe as merchant of record, those intermediaries may hold the global VAT/GST registration obligations for the underlying supply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or comparable entity classification election exists under Gibraltar or Cayman law. The former Gibraltar 'Qualifying Offshore Company' election was abolished; the current default is entity-level taxation at 10% corporation tax for companies resident and managed or controlled in Gibraltar, with non-resident companies taxed only on Gibraltar-source income. The Cayman Exempted Company cannot elect to be transparent or disregarded for Gibraltar tax purposes. Hybrid mismatch principles under Gibraltar's Income Tax Act, aligned with OECD and UK rules, treat the Cayman company as a separate opaque legal entity, not as a pass-through.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT/GST Not Applicable; Gibraltar Purchase Tax (tax on physical goods only)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for Gibraltar Purchase Tax: registration is event-driven on the first import of chargeable goods into Gibraltar. For UK VAT, if the Cayman entity itself makes taxable supplies of remote digital services to UK consumers through a UK establishment or at source, the then-current UK VAT registration threshold of £85,000 (2024/25) applies only to UK-established businesses; non-established suppliers generally have no threshold and must register for UK VAT from the first supply unless using an eligible non-UK OSS scheme or relying on the merchant of record.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, tax API, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mandate. Purchase Tax is declared through customs entries; corporate income tax is filed annually via the Income Tax Office. If the entity later registers for UK VAT, it must maintain digital VAT records and submit returns through Making Tax Digital (MTD)-compatible software using HMRC APIs; electronic invoicing is permitted but not mandatory. Third-party merchant-of-record providers (Stripe, Paddle) may issue tax-compliant VAT/GST invoices on behalf of the supplier in foreign jurisdictions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable to the core software supply: Gibraltar Purchase Tax and Cayman customs duty apply only to physical goods. Electronically supplied remote screen-share and IoT telemetry software is an intangible service outside the scope of Gibraltar Purchase Tax; therefore no zero-rating claim exists. If the Cayman entity becomes UK VAT registered, supplies of digital services to non-UK business customers are outside the scope of UK VAT under place-of-supply rules, while supplies to UK consumers are standard-rated. Export zero-rating under UK VAT is reserved for tangible exported goods and requires proof of physical removal from the UK within the statutory time limit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration/Entry (electronic Single Administrative Document or export declaration reference)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (proof of physical removal from the UK/Gibraltar for tangible exports)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/FX receipt evidencing receipt of export consideration from the overseas buyer
Commercial Invoice (for exported goods or the invoiced service)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating or export VAT refund claims, if the entity has UK VAT exposure, are prosecuted by HMRC under the Value Added Tax Act 1994: civil penalties up to 100% of the tax at risk for deliberate inaccuracy, fraud penalties, and criminal liability for dishonest evasion are possible. Retrospective recovery generally extends to 4 years for careless inaccuracies and 20 years for deliberate concealment. In Gibraltar, evasion of Purchase Tax may result in Customs seizure, monetary penalties up to twice the duty, and criminal prosecution; no Purchase Tax refund mechanism exists for exported goods because the tax is charged at the import stage, and the Cayman entity has no entitlement to export refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (monetary authority for Sterling) and Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as the local banking and forex supervisory authority; Gibraltar has no separate central bank and the Gibraltar Pound is issued by the Government of Gibraltar under a currency board arrangement pegged at par to GBP.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar maintains full current and capital account convertibility. The Gibraltar Pound is freely convertible at a fixed 1:1 parity with GBP, and there are no restrictions on the conversion of USD, EUR, or other major currencies. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and capital repatriation are permitted without prior regulatory approval or withholding in Gibraltar. For the Cayman Exempted Company, no Cayman Exchange Control restrictions apply; however, the entity must avoid management-and-control being exercised from Gibraltar to prevent inadvertent Gibraltar tax residence. The key profit remittance hurdle arises from UK anti-money laundering and economic substance documentation expectations, not from FX restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio exists for export proceeds in Gibraltar. Export receipts can be retained in any convertible currency, and there is no requirement to surrender foreign currency to the Government of Gibraltar or the Bank of England. The Cayman Islands also impose no export surrender rules. The only applicable obligations relate to record-keeping and AML transaction reporting for cross-border receipts routed through UK or EU payment systems, which require end-to-end beneficiary and purpose-code transparency.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for major UK/EU EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex, and Currencycloud when combined with a Gibraltar-licensed corporate service provider as introducer. Legal constraints: Gibraltar is not a member of the EU single passporting regime for payment services; an EEA-licensed EMI cannot passport into Gibraltar. The Cayman Exempted Company is treated as high-risk by most EMIs due to its tax-exempt offshore status and should therefore establish a Gibraltar branch or a locally regulated payment services entity to access full clearing rails. An FCA-registered EMI relationship is permitted only if the EMI obtains a variation of permission or Gibraltar approval for the intended cross-border payment activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance is generally required at the bank premises for directors of a foreign Cayman Exempted Company. The GFSC AML Guidance permits a remote video interview under strict conditions: the interview must be conducted by a locally licensed compliance officer, the corporate KYC package must be notarised by a Gibraltar Notary, and the Cayman registered agent must provide a certificate of incumbency and a register of members with no bearer shares. Given the target entity is a Cayman Exempted Company with no physical presence, remote onboarding is conditionally available only if the UBO is an individual who appears by video with two forms of identification and proof of address, and a Gibraltar-licensed corporate service provider serves as introducer and AML gatekeeper.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman exempted company with historical bearer shares or nominee shareholder arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current certificate of incumbency from Cayman registered agent; full register of members evidencing that every share is registered in a named natural or corporate holder; express declaration that no bearer shares exist; Cayman Beneficial Ownership Register (DISS) filing confirmation; signed indemnity from the beneficial owner waiving anonymity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore company with no economic substance in Gibraltar and no local office
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cayman Exemption Certificate under Section 6 of the Companies Act (GCS); tax residence opinion from a reputable law firm confirming management and control is outside Gibraltar; board meeting minutes evidencing decision-making in the Cayman Islands or another jurisdiction; detailed substance documentation for the remote-support software operations, including licences, staff contracts outside Gibraltar, and a commercial agency agreement with a Gibraltar third-party service provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business description perceived as high cyber-risk (unattended remote access software)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sector classification showing ISIC 6201 and NAICS 511210; ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate; SOC 2 Type II report; cybersecurity insurance policy; written confirmation that the software is used solely for lawful remote support, not for covert monitoring; customer onboarding KYC and acceptable-use policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment flows through third-party gemisons (Stripe/Paddle) without a regulated payment institution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant agreements from Stripe and Paddle naming the Cayman Exempted Company as merchant of record; evidence that the PSPs obtain customer KYC details; monthly settlement reports reconciling gross revenues and transaction identifiers; Gibraltar tax and business compliance confirmation that funds received offshore are not taxable under Gibraltar domestic law.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection from the Cayman parent to the Gibraltar operating account must follow a strictly documented wire protocol: (i) adopt a board resolution in Cayman authorising the share capital contribution and identifying the exact amount in GBP or USD; (ii) open a segregated Capital Escrow Account in Gibraltar in the name of the Cayman Exempted Company; (iii) transmit via SWIFT MT103 from a licensed Cayman bank (e.g., Butterfield Bank (Cayman) or Cayman National Bank) to the Gibraltar receiving bank, using SWIFT purpose code CAIT (Capital Investment) or their operational equivalent for direct investment; (iv) ensure the payment narrative includes the corporate registration number, beneficiary name, and explicit phrase 'Capital Injection - Unpaid Capital under Cayman Companies Act (Exempted Company)'; (v) provide the Gibraltar receiving bank with a copy of the resolution, a source-of-funds statement showing the Cayman bank account history, and confirmation that no funds originate from the sale of negotiable bearer instruments. All funds should clear via the correspondent banking network: GBP via CHAPS in London, USD via CHIPS/Fedwire, EUR via SEPA or TARGET2.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements from the Gibraltar operating account to global suppliers, contractors, tax authorities, and the Cayman parent must use the following clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for high-value or one-off invoices, with proper purpose codes (e.g., 'Software licensing fees', 'Subcontractor services', 'Dividend distribution') and the beneficiary bank's BIC; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary UCP 600) for hardware procurements connected to IoT telemetry devices, issued by the Gibraltar bank against pro-forma invoices and transport documents; (iii) SEPA credit transfers for low-value EUR obligations within the EEA; (iv) intercompany profit distributions to the Cayman parent via MT103 using purpose code 'DIV' and accompanied by a distribution certificate. The customer-facing settlement rails from Stripe/Paddle are aggregated and settled to the Gibraltar account via daily MT103 sweeps from the PSP's corporate bank, which must be reconciled against merchant statement data.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards (standard maturity 1-24 months) on GBP/USD and EUR/USD with the onboarded Gibraltar bank

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or low-liquidity currencies (e.g., CNY, INR) executed only through a licensed non-bank financial counterparty and subject to professional-client classification

Cross-currency swaps (basis swaps or fixed-float) for balance-sheet hedging of the USD-denominated Cayman capital against GBP/EUR operating expenses, restricted to a one-to-one notional matching the actual asset exposure

No options, binary options, or structured FX products may be used without prior written approval from the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission and explicit classification as a professional/eligible counterparty

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% (Gibraltar standard corporate income tax rate); 0% statutory corporate income tax in the Cayman Islands for an Exempted Company that is not tax-resident in Gibraltar and has no Gibraltar permanent establishment. The composite structure is analysed as a Cayman Exempted Company whose central management and control is exercised from Gibraltar, therefore a Gibraltar tax-resident software company for the purposes of this whitepaper.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Gibraltar: no general statutory tax holiday; the pre-2015 tax exempt company status was abolished with effect from 1 July 2015 and existing exempt companies were grandfathered only to 30 June 2016. Available reliefs: 100% first-year capital allowances on qualifying green technology and telemetry hardware, R&D expenditure uplift, participation-style dividend exemption on substantial shareholdings, and loss relief. Cayman Islands: nil effective corporation tax at all times; only annual government registration fees (approx. USD 576 for registered capital not exceeding USD 50,000 and USD 1,488 for capital above USD 1 million) plus ESR annual compliance costs apply.
